Speaker: The Wanderer
When it's heard: Prologue: waking up in the forest
Current line: Ugh... where am I? And while I'm asking, who am I?
New line: Where... where is this? I can smell wet leaves, and my head feels as if someone has packed it with wool.

Speaker: The Wanderer
When it's heard: Prologue: waking up in the forest
Current line: I keep reaching for my name, or for how I got here, and there's nothing there at all.
New line: I keep reaching for my name, and it isn't there. Neither is how I came to be here. There's nothing at all, like a room that somebody has emptied.

Speaker: The Wanderer
When it's heard: Prologue: waking up in the forest
Current line: I should get up. My legs have other ideas, and every part of me aches.
New line: I ought to try standing up, though my legs don't seem to agree, and I ache in places I couldn't even put a name to.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: A cold draft rises out of the dark, smelling of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town lies on the other side. Go in?
New line: A cold draft rises out of the dark, and it smells of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town lies on the other side of this cave. Go in?

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Easy. Stay down a moment and get your breath back. After what they put you through, I'm amazed you're breathing at all.
New line: Easy, now. Stay down for a moment and get your breath back. After what they put you through, I'm amazed you're breathing at all.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: And keep your voice low. We're not the only ones in these woods tonight.
New line: Keep your voice low, though. We aren't the only ones in these woods tonight, and the others aren't looking for you out of kindness.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: I don't know this place, and I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?
New line: I don't know this place. I don't even know my own name. ...Who are you?

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: A friend. That's all I can tell you, and there isn't time for more.
New line: A friend. I know that isn't much of an answer, and I'm sorry. It's the only one I can give you tonight.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Can you still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand and let me see.
New line: Can you still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand and let me see. Gently, I only want to look.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: ...I feel them. All four, faintly. Like voices through a wall.
New line: ...I can feel them. All four of them, but faintly, like voices through a wall.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: That will have to do. The Path-ologists are hunting us.
New line: Then they didn't manage to take everything. That will have to do for now, because the Path-ologists are already out hunting for us.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: That one, then. Hold on to it. The others will come back to you, in time.
New line: That one, then. Hold on to it as tightly as you can. The others will come back to you in time; I'm almost sure of it.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Hear that? They're close, but they don't know about the cave. Hardly anyone remembers it now.
New line: Do you hear that? They're close, but they don't know about the cave. Hardly anyone remembers it's here any more.

Speaker: The Rescuer
Current line: Go, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and when I'm clear, I'll find you. I always do.
New line: Go now, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and once I'm clear of them, I'll find you. I always do.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: She's gone, and she's taking the shouting with her. Whoever they are, I'd rather not meet them.
New line: She's gone, and the shouting has gone after her. I don't know who those people are, but I'd rather not be standing here when they come back.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: The trees are packed too tight to get through. The cave it is, then.
New line: The trees are packed too tightly to squeeze through here. It will have to be the cave, then.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: No point getting lost twice in one day. I'll head back up the path to the glowing arch.
New line: There's no sense in getting lost twice in one day. I'll go back up the path to the glowing arch.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: Whatever is waiting for me, it's through that cave.
New line: Whatever is waiting for me, it's on the other side of that cave.

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: Whoever she was, she said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever's in that cave, it has to be better than those Path-ologists.
New line: She said someone would be waiting on the other side, whoever she was. And whatever is in that cave, it can't be worse than those Path-ologists.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: ...Footsteps. It has been a long time since anything woke me.
New line: ...Footsteps. It has been a long time since anything came down here to wake me.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: No one has walked this way since the house fell silent. I have kept the door all the same.
New line: No one has walked this way since the house above fell silent. I have kept the door all the same, for there was no one left to tell me that I might stop.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: Turn back. Only one may pass this door, and he is long dead.
New line: Turn back, traveller. Only one may pass this door, and he is long dead.

Speaker: Hollow Warden
When it's heard: Mid-fight event "The Warden Stirs" vs Hollow Warden: the foe says it when the event fires
Current line: ...That light in your hands. I know it. No. NO. You cannot be him. He is gone.
New line: ...That light in your hands. I have seen that light before. No... no, you cannot be him. He is gone. He has been gone so long.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: ...The door knows your hand. I do not understand it, but I will not stand against it. Pass, and let the Paths guide you.
New line: ...The door knows your hand. I do not understand how that can be, but I was not left here to understand. Pass, and may the Paths guide you home.

Speaker: The Hollow Warden
Current line: The light goes out of the Warden's eyes slowly, like a lamp turned down for the night.
New line: The light goes out of the Warden's eyes slowly, like a lamp turned down for the night by someone who means to come back to it.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: You wake in a forest clearing with leaves in your hair.
New line: You wake in a forest clearing with leaves in your hair, and no idea how long you have been lying there.

Speaker: (narration)
Current line: A faint glow of four colors fades from your hand, like a thought you almost had.
New line: A faint glow of four colors is fading from your hand, like a thought you almost had.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Hmph. About time. {villain}'s soldiers have been up and down the road all day, and nobody has come out of that cave in ten years, so forgive me for staring.
New line: Hmph. About time. {villain}'s soldiers have been up and down that road all day, and nobody has come out of this cave in ten years, so you'll have to forgive an old tortoise for staring.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: And look at the state of you. I told her I'd help whoever she sent along. I never said I'd take in a half-drowned stray.
New line: And just look at the state of you. I told her I would help whoever she sent along, but I don't recall agreeing to take in a half-drowned stray who can barely stand.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: I didn't want any part of this, and I told her so. She went ahead anyway. She always does.
New line: I didn't want any part of this, and I told her so to her face. She went and did it anyway. She always does, that one.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: But you need a bed, and I've baked far too much pie, so I can hardly leave you out here on your own, can I?
New line: Still, you need a bed, and I've gone and baked far too much pie again, so I can hardly leave you standing out here on your own, can I?

Speaker: The Wanderer
Current line: I don't know who I am, or where this is. I don't even know the name of the woman who got me out.
New line: I'm sorry to be a trouble. I don't know who I am, or where this is. I don't even know the name of the woman who got me out.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Hm. If she didn't give you her name, she had a reason, and I won't be the one to spoil it. As for where you are: this is {town}. We settle most things here with cards, and I see you've already got a deck.
New line: Hm. If she didn't give you her name, she'll have had her reasons, and I won't be the one to spoil them. As for where you are, this is {town}. We settle most things here with cards, and I see you've brought a deck.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: If your memory's really gone, you'll be here a while, so you'd best get to know people. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, buy yourself a card from Sable, then come back to me.
New line: If your memory really is gone, you'll be with us a while, so you'd best get to know people. Go and say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, buy yourself a card from Sable, and then come back to me.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: One more thing before you go dripping on somebody else's floor. That deck of yours is {path} through and through. When the time comes to go out on the roads, {zone} will be the easiest one for you.
New line: One more thing, before you go dripping on anybody else's floor. That deck of yours is {path} through and through, so when the time comes to go out on the roads, {zone} will be the easiest one for you.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: But not yet. Every road out of town has a gatekeeper standing across it, and you're in no state to argue with any of them. Settle in first: meet the shopkeepers, and let me give you a few errands to learn the ropes.
New line: But not yet. Every road out of town has a gatekeeper standing across it, and you're in no state to argue with any of them. Settle in first: meet the shopkeepers, and let me give you an errand or two to learn the ropes.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Come and find me on the square once you've dried off. When you're ready, I'll send you out myself.
New line: Come and find me on the square once you've dried off. When you're ready for the roads, I'll send you out myself.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)
Current line: Up and walking. Good. I am Elder Maren, dearie, and this is {town}, where the four Paths used to meet, and argue, and borrow each other's pans.
New line: Up and walking, I see. Good. I'm Elder Maren, dearie, and this is {town}, where the four Paths used to meet, and argue, and borrow each other's pans and never give them back.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)
Current line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes kept the lights on, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead and Refusemancers turned rubbish into harvests. Everyone complained, and everything worked.
New line: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes kept the lights on, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers turned rubbish into harvests. Four peoples who never matched, stitched together, and it held.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)
Current line: Then {villain}, the Minister of Improvements, took the Paths one by one and set his own people over them. Now every road out of town has a gatekeeper: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.
New line: Then {villain}, the Minister of Improvements, took the Paths one at a time and set his own people over them. Now every road out of town has a gatekeeper across it: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door and a wall of thorns.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (first)
Current line: Beat a road's gatekeeper and that road opens. Before you try, buy a few cards from Sable and sort your deck at the Deck Station. Then come back to me for pie. Pie, mind. Not answers.
New line: Beat a road's gatekeeper and that road opens. Before you try, buy a few cards from Sable and sort your deck out at the Deck Station. Then come back to me for pie. Pie, mind you, and not answers. I'm short of those.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (return)
Current line: Four roads out of town, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. Pick one and see it through before you start the next.
New line: There are four roads out of town, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. Pick one and see it through to the end before you start on the next.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (return)
Current line: For all I know, you're somebody's spy. I've been wrong about people before, and it cost more than I like to think about.
New line: For all I know you're somebody's spy, and here I am feeding you. I've been wrong about people before, you see, and it cost more than I like to think about.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Still here, dearie? {villain} would like nothing better than you sitting by my fire forever, so don't give him the satisfaction. And give me back my chair.
New line: Still here, dearie? {villain} would like nothing better than you sat by my fire for good, so let's not oblige him. Besides, you're in my chair.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: The pie on the sill needs another hour, dearie. You don't. Off you go.
New line: The pie on the sill wants another hour, dearie, and you don't. Off you go, and it'll be ready when you're back.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: If you're looking for advice: eat something. If you're looking for more advice: eat something else.
New line: If it's advice you're after, eat something. And if you were hoping for better advice than that, eat something else as well.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: I've given you all the answers you need for now, dearie. Further questions require fieldwork.
New line: I've told you all I can for now, dearie. The rest you'll have to go out and find for yourself, and I'd only slow you down.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Mind the fountain, dearie. People throw wishes in it. Most of them are mine.
New line: Mind the fountain as you go, dearie. People throw their wishes into it, and over the years a good many of them have been mine.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (idle)
Current line: Off you go, dearie. I'll be here when you get back. Tortoises are very dependable, just not quickly.
New line: Off you go, dearie. I'll be right here when you get back. We tortoises are very dependable, so long as nobody's in a hurry.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 0)
Current line: I still don't know what to make of you, dearie. But you need feeding more than you need questioning, so sit down a minute.
New line: I still don't know what to make of you, dearie. But you need feeding a good deal more than you need questioning, so sit yourself down for a minute.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 0)
Current line: Have as much pie as you like. Just keep your eyes off the recipe; better people than you have tried.
New line: Have as much pie as you like. Just keep your eyes off the recipe card. Better people than you have tried for it, and I caught every one of them.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 1)
Current line: That tune's stayed with you, hasn't it? I can see it on your face. Good. Keep it somewhere safe, dearie, even when it hurts.
New line: That tune has stayed with you, hasn't it? I can see it in your face. Good. Keep it somewhere safe, dearie, even on the days when it hurts to hear.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 1)
Current line: Found any more answers out there? I keep telling myself it's none of my business, and I keep asking anyway.
New line: Have you found any more answers out there? I keep telling myself it's none of my business, and then I keep asking anyway.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 2)
Current line: Somebody in the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'That's no prince,' I told them. 'That's a damp young man with good posture.' Don't look so startled, dearie.
New line: Somebody on the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'That's no prince,' I told them. 'That's a damp young man with good posture.' Oh, don't look so startled, dearie.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 2)
Current line: When you find Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue, and she'll be wrong.
New line: When you find Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in this kingdom. She'll argue with you, and she'll be wrong, and it'll do her good to hear it all the same.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 3)
Current line: I have told you the worst of me. The rest is easy, by comparison.
New line: Well, I've told you the worst of me now. Whatever else I have to say to you will come easily, after that.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 3)
Current line: Go on, dearie. The next road won't open itself, and if we left it to me, we'd be at it until the regime died of old age.
New line: Go on, dearie. That last road won't open by itself, and if it were left to me to walk there, the regime would die of old age first.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 4)
Current line: {prince}. I keep wanting to curtsy. My knees have voted against it.
New line: {prince}. I keep wanting to curtsy when you come in, and my knees keep voting against it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (stage 4)
Current line: Go on, then. The kingdom has waited ten years for you; the pie won't wait ten minutes.
New line: Go on, then. The kingdom has waited ten years for you and can manage one more hour, but this pie won't keep for ten minutes.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (known early)
Current line: {prince}. {villain} let it slip to you, didn't he, that smug man. I had hoped to tell you myself.
New line: {prince}. So {villain} let it slip, did he, the smug creature. I had hoped you would hear it from me, in a warm kitchen, and not from him.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Talking to Elder Maren in Crosspath (known early)
Current line: Sit down. The rest of your memories will come when they're ready, and I'll be right here when they do. With pie, obviously.
New line: Sit down. The rest of your memories will come when they're ready, and I'll be right here when they do, with a pie in the oven. I'm not going anywhere.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Meet the Merchants": while it is active
Current line: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all three on the square. And buy a card from Sable while you're there. I'll not have you facing the roads with nothing but what a cave gave you.
New line: It's Sable, Tilly and Pip you want, dearie, all three of them on the square. And buy a card from Sable while you're there. I won't have you facing the roads with nothing but what a cave gave you.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Meet the Merchants": handing it in
Current line: Back already? Let me guess: Sable charmed you, Tilly turned a colour, and Pip measured you before you'd finished saying hello. That's {town}, dearie.
New line: Back already? Let me guess: Sable charmed you, Tilly turned a new colour, and Pip had you measured before you'd finished saying hello. That's {town} for you, dearie, and you'll get used to it.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: New cards first, so open a pack: the Menu at the top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you're the sort who presses things.
New line: You'll want some new cards first, so open a pack: that's the Menu at the top right, then Packs. Or you can press P, if you're the sort who likes pressing things.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Then take it to the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap in whatever you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me how it went.
New line: Then take it all down to the Deck Station, on Champions' Road south of the square. Swap in whatever takes your fancy, save the deck to a slot, and come and tell me how it went.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Make It Yours": when offered (pack step)
Current line: No packs at all? Here, dearie, have a General Pack. It's been sat on a little. Cards are cards, and these ones won't hold it against you.
New line: No packs at all? Here, dearie, take this General Pack. It's been sat on a little, I'm afraid, but cards are cards, and these ones won't hold it against you.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Make It Yours": while active (pack step)
Current line: Open the pack first, dearie: the Menu, then Packs. It won't open itself. I've asked it nicely.
New line: Open the pack first, dearie: the Menu, then Packs. It won't open itself. I should know, because I've asked it nicely.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Make It Yours": while it is active
Current line: The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square, dearie. Save it to a slot when you're done, or it doesn't count. I do check.
New line: The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square, dearie. Remember to save the deck to a slot when you're done, or it doesn't count. And I do check.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Make It Yours": handing it in
Current line: Sorted and saved, and every card in it your own choice. Good. Now when it loses, you've nobody to blame but yourself, which is how it ought to be.
New line: Sorted and saved, and every card in it one you chose for yourself. Good. Now when it loses, you'll have nobody to blame but you, which is exactly how it ought to be.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": when offered
Current line: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been cold and whispering for a week. I don't mean Tilly, dearie. I mean the room.
New line: Now, I've a favour to ask of you. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been cold and whispering for a week. I don't mean Tilly, dearie. I mean the room.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": when offered
Current line: Ghosts, I expect, and old ones. The Tonics have kept that room locked since before I came to Crosspath, and I've never asked them why. Go and see what wants out, and be gentle with it if it lets you.
New line: Ghosts, I expect, and old ones. The Tonics have kept that door locked since before I came to Crosspath, and I've never asked them why. Go and see what wants out, and be gentle with it, if it lets you be.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": while it is active
Current line: The store room door is beside Tilly's shop, on the north side of the square. If there are marks on the frame, leave them be, dearie. Somebody put them there for a reason.
New line: The store room door is beside Tilly's shop, on the north side of the square. If there are marks painted on the frame, leave them be, dearie. Whoever put them there had a reason.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": handing it in
Current line: Gone, are they? Good. No, I don't want to hear what they said. Not out here on the square, and not before supper.
New line: They've gone, have they? Good. No, I don't want to hear what they said to you, not out here on the square and certainly not before my supper.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": handing it in
Current line: Tilly's family were healers, mostly. Mostly. Some of the old families kept a back room for the other kind of remedy, and the less said about it, the better for Tilly. She's a good girl, and none of it is hers.
New line: Tilly's family were healers, mostly. Only mostly. Some of the old families kept a back room for the other sort of remedy, and the less said of it the better for Tilly. She's a good girl, and none of that is hers.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Something in the Store Room": handing it in
Current line: Well done, dearie. Now go and sit somewhere warm for a bit. You've gone the colour of a candle.
New line: You did well, dearie, and I hear you were kind about it. Now go and sit somewhere warm for a while, because you've gone the colour of a candle.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Right, then. It's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth hands out gear from his smithy, on the west side of the square.
New line: Right, then. It's high time you had something sharper than a deck of cards. Bertram Beetsworth hands out the gear from his smithy, on the west side of the square.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: He is... thorough. Report to him, do what he asks, and do not touch his drawer.
New line: He is... thorough, shall we say. Report to him, do exactly what he asks of you, and whatever else you do, don't touch his drawer.

Speaker: Elder Maren
When it's heard: Quest "Some Assembly Required": while it is active
Current line: Bertram's smithy is on the west side of the square. Win him one fight, any fight at all, and he'll stamp something for you. He lives to stamp things.
New line: Bertram's smithy is on the west side of the square. Win him one fight, any fight at all, and he'll stamp something for you. That man lives to stamp things.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: There you are, and with a blade on your belt at last. Bertram tells me you didn't even cut yourself. I'm impressed, dearie, and I don't impress easily.
New line: There you are, and with a blade on your belt at last. Bertram tells me you didn't even cut yourself, and I'm impressed, dearie. I don't impress easily.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: You've met the shopkeepers, sorted out your deck, sent the things in Tilly's store room packing and got yourself kitted out. That's all the settling in I can teach you. Now I need you out on the roads.
New line: You've met the shopkeepers, made that deck your own, been gentle with whatever was in Tilly's store room and got yourself kitted out. That's all the settling in I know how to teach. Now I need you out on the roads.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: I've put all four gatekeepers in your quest log, with yours on top. Go on, then, and come back alive. I'll have a pie waiting, and I don't bake for people who don't come back.
New line: I've put all four gatekeepers in your quest log, with yours at the top. Go on, then, and come back in one piece. There'll be a pie waiting, and I don't bake for people who don't come back.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: You've gone pale as flour. Sit down, sit. Something's come back to you, hasn't it?
New line: You've gone as pale as flour. Sit down, sit down. Something has come back to you, hasn't it?

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: Tell me all of it, however small it seems. The small things are usually the ones that matter.
New line: Tell me all of it, however small it seems to you. In my experience it's the small things that turn out to matter.

Speaker: (narration/UI)
Current line: Light. Four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.
New line: There is light, four colors of it, as warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.

Speaker: (narration/UI)
Current line: A woman is humming a tune with no words, and it rises and falls like someone breathing in their sleep.
New line: A woman is humming a tune with no words to it, and it rises and falls like someone breathing in their sleep.

Speaker: (narration/UI)
Current line: Then the light thins, like breath on glass, and I am back.
New line: Then the light thins, like breath on glass, and I am back beside the fire.

Speaker: Elder Maren
Current line: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days, from the court, and there are very few left who remember it. Fewer still who'd hum it.
New line: ...A lullaby. That tune comes from the old days, from the court, and there are very few of us left who would know it. Fewer still who ever hummed it to a child.

Speaker: Prudence Pallor, Checkpoint Supervisor

New line: Archdruid Compostella is herself again, and she hugged me! She smells of rain, and a little bit of compost, which is exactly how an Archdruid ought to smell.

Speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
When it's heard: Gatekeeper of the Verdant Dump: talking at the gate

New line: Would you like a practice round? I'll try very hard not to thorn at you. The raccoons have come to watch, so we had both better be on our best behaviour.

Speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid

Speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid

Speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex

New line: Quietly, son. The guards time their rounds by counting their own squats, and sooner or later every one of them loses count.

Speaker: The Wanderer

New line: You're Grandmaster Flex? Everyone up there talks about you as though you were twice this size.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex

New line: Ten years in the dark will do that to a man. They took my plates and my protein and every bar I ever lifted, and they left me down here with nothing at all.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex
Current line: And nothing, it turns out, is a fine place to start. I still had my breath, my body and my mind, so I trained them every day.
New line: And nothing, it turns out, is a fine place to start from. I still had my breath, my body and my mind, so I trained those, every day.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex
Current line: Come, son, we'll climb out together. I'd like a word with Clench on the way. He was the best student I ever had. He still is.
New line: Come along, son, and we'll climb out of here together. I'd like a word with Clench on the way. He was the best student I ever had, you know. He still is.

Speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
When it's heard: Dungeon node "hg boss": entering the node

New line: "Master." The word sticks in his throat. "I was your best, you know. Your star pupil. You said so yourself."

Speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent

New line: "You told me I would go further than you ever did. And then you started on about strength living in the heart and the head, and I knew better than that."

Speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
When it's heard: Dungeon node "hg boss": entering the node
Current line: "I took your iron, your protein and your followers, and you've climbed back up here with nothing, Master."
New line: "So I took your iron, and your protein, and your followers, and here you are, climbing back up my stairs with nothing at all."

Speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
When it's heard: Dungeon node "hg boss": entering the node
Current line: "Look how far I went, Master. What exactly do you think you can do about it now?"
New line: "Look how far I went, Master. What exactly do you imagine you can do about it now?"

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex

New line: Stand back a little, son, if you would. It has been a long time, and I should like some room.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex

New line: You only ever wanted the weight, my boy. I was trying to teach you the heart, and you stopped listening long before I ever got to the mind.

Speaker: Chancellor Clench
Current line: ...How? Ten years in a hole with nothing - where were you HIDING all of that?
New line: ...How? Ten years in a hole with nothing. Where were you HIDING all of that?

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex

New line: Strength was never a matter of how heavy a thing is, Clench. It lives in the heart and the mind, and nobody can lock those in a cell.

New line: Flex doesn't gloat. He kneels beside his fallen pupil and holds out a hand. "You hated yourself for needing the iron, my boy."

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken

New line: "I never once hated you for it. Come back to the gym. We'll start from zero, the way everyone does."

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken

New line: Quota's gone. She was off to the Capital before the dust had even settled; she always did like to leave early.

Speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken

New line: We'll keep her schedule, because it will make good kindling. And breathe, son. Nobody in this house is on the clock any more.

New line: The Grand Chef turns from the stove wearing the same smile as every portrait in the Pantry. In ten years, it has never once creased.

Speaker: The Doppelganger

New line: Welcome to the Executive Test Kitchen, taster. Ten years I have worn this face and this apron, and not one Gourmand ever looked twice.

Speaker: The Doppelganger

New line: ...Tasting is inefficient. The orders from {capital} asked for golems and not for flavour, and the Special Sauce delivers golems.

New line: This is what was underneath. I wore her face for so long that I forgot my own, and there is nothing in here to taste with.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: Ten years in a freezer, and I can still remember exactly what this soup ought to taste like. Out of my way, and let me put it right.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: Stand back, the lot of you. Somebody fetch me flour and butter, and light the biggest oven in this building.

Speaker: The Endless Buffet

New line: Before you sits a plain golden dish, large enough to share, and it smells of butter and warm bread.

Speaker: The Endless Buffet

New line: The first bite breaks the enchantment, all the way through the Endless Buffet.

Speaker: The Endless Buffet

New line: The chefs stand blinking at their own hands, and all across the Buffet a thousand golems lower their ladles.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Current line: You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Today you start, and I'll give you something to start with.
New line: You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Well, today you start, and I'll give you something to start with.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Current line: Take my old name, then: Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title, and the name could do with someone starting fresh.
New line: Take my old name: Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title, and that name could do with somebody making a fresh start in it.

Speaker: Escoffina
Current line: ...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly. I will try to be someone worth the name.
New line: ...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly. I will try to be somebody worth the name.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: Have you eaten? Sit, sit. I'm the Grand Chef, and you'll have to forgive the apron. The impostor kept it cleaner than I do, but I wear it with more feeling.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: Ten years in the walk-in freezer, and I never once forgot the taste of honest soup. And all that time they were putting that sauce in every pot and calling it innovation.

Speaker: The Grand Chef
Current line: Thank you for finding me. Now eat.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: Let me cook for you properly. I promise there's nothing in it but food.

Speaker: The Grand Chef

New line: And you, my dear, don't know your own name yet. That isn't a flaw, it's a blank page. Go and do something worth signing.

Zone/Area: D.N.A. / The Hall of Final Approvals

New line: Me? Oh, for pity's sake. I filed more appeals than anybody, living or dead, and this is what they give me for it?

Zone/Area: D.N.A. / The Hall of Final Approvals
Speaker: Agnes Overdue

Speaker: Agnes Overdue

New line: Agnes Overdue, head of the D.N.A. Yes, dear, me. The office goes to the senior-most applicant, and I filed more appeals than anyone. I have never been so annoyed to win anything.

New line: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I am the one who outlawed composting. All that rot lying about in heaps, being honest with everybody. So untidy.

New line: It's the seed, {villain}'s gift: life that never dies. I grew up beneath a great tree, child, and when she fell, I couldn't bear it.

New line: Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease, and we're the Wrinkles: the people {villain} couldn't iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea's better.

Speaker: Wren

Speaker: Wren
Current line: He's afraid of everything that won't obey him. It's a small, sad fear for a man with so much gold.
New line: He is afraid of everything that won't obey him. It's a small, sad sort of fear, for a man with so much gold.

Speaker: Wren
Current line: That's all four, and I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.

Speaker: Wren

New line: He is a man who made a list of everything he couldn't control, and then made every item on it illegal.

New line: The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we will know.
